day: The Exaltation of the Holy Cross ‐ Feast
text:
In the wilderness, the people faced their own mortality and grew afraid. God did not remove the danger, but gave them a way to live within it: they had only to look. This strange mercy—a bronze serpent raised on a pole—became their salvation. All they needed was to see it, to acknowledge what was there, and to trust.

Jesus tells us he is lifted up in the same way. The cross, like that ancient standard in the desert, is not the absence of suffering but its transformation into a path toward life. When we look upon it—really look, with honesty about our own brokenness and need—we encounter not condemnation but love. God so loved the world that he entered into our deepest struggle, not to shame us but to show us the way through.

The deeds of the Lord are worth remembering. They tell us that God does not abandon us in our wilderness, but meets us there. He invites us to look, to believe, to live. What does it mean for you, today, to look toward the cross with trust?
